messages:
Ashley (eng-runtime): Running a quick nsys capture on the nightly load; noticed odd KV cache shadowing where we get a ~12% effective hitdrop for short prefixes. Attached trace link: https://perf.internal/nsys/1851234567
Mike R.: hmm 12% is... higher than I'd expect for the short prompt set. Is this only on the 2k sequence tests?
Ashley (eng-runtime): Repro across 512 and 2k, but pattern different. For 512 we see more frequent kernel switches (matmul->softmax) that evict prefix entries earlier. Trace snapshot: 
```
GPU timeline: kernel matmul_a (0.32ms) -> kernel softmax_b (0.08ms) -> memcpy kv_load (0.12ms)
KV cache events: load_hit=84 load_miss=16 (sample window)
Batch policy: adaptive_batch_v2 enabled
```
Jordan T.: do you have the raw kernel names? matmul_a vs matmul_a_fused? we changed selection heuristics last week to prefer fused kernels at seqlen<128, could be a mismatch.
Ashley (eng-runtime): Good point. Raw logs show matmul_a_fused used intermittently; I think the runtime sometimes falls back to matmul_a when batch consolidation happens. That fallback aligns with the times we lose KV cache locality.
Lee (ML perf): That fallback could change register pressure and memory access pattern, causing prefix cache lines to be evicted sooner. Can you grep for kernel selection decisions in the trace? nsys with --trace=cuda,nvtx should have kernel selection markers.
Ashley (eng-runtime): I re-ran with NVTX markers, extracted a short timeline and annotated: 
```
[0.1234] REQUEST_START id=4273
[0.1240] select_kernel(model=tiny-llm, seqlen=64) -> matmul_a_fused
[0.1243] runtime->batch_consolidate: merge (2 requests) -> promote kernel -> matmul_a
[0.1245] KV_CACHE_EVICT id=pref_309 idx=12
[0.1246] kernel matmul_a start
```
So consolidation triggers non-deterministic kernel choice.
Mike R.: Consolidation algorithm picks kernel by aggregated seq distribution; if two requests have different preferred kernels we might pick the cheaper average. That could be a bug: we should prefer the kernel that preserves KV locality for prefixes when one request is prefix-heavy.
perf-bot: automated-check: recent commit 9f4b1 changed batch_heuristic to aggressive_merge=true. Regression probability: medium.
Jordan T.: can we add a quick guard: when any request in the batch has KV_prefix_size>0, bias selection to kernel that preserves KV alignment? Simple weighted cost function.
Ashley (eng-runtime): I prototyped a patch that adds prefix_weight=+0.25 to the kernel scoring. On a microbenchmark it drops hitdrop from 12% -> 3% and p50 latency improves ~6%. Full nightly run in progress (will post results).
Lee (ML perf): Nice. Also curious if prefetch/prefill timings change: maybe we should insert a small KV prefetch after consolidation if fallback kernel chosen, to warm lines before compute. Could be a cheap win.
Mike R.: Prefetch is worth trying but beware increased memory bandwidth. For short prefixes prefetch might be cheaper than extra kernel switching. Add config flag runtime.kv_prefetch_on_fallback=false by default.
Ashley (eng-runtime): Will push the kernel-bias + runtime flag to review. Also stacking request-level NVTX tags so perfetto can show which request caused eviction.
Jordan T.: Also add a reproducer script in eng-runtime/tools that runs 1000 randomized short-prefixed requests with deterministic RNG so we can assert hitrate.
Ashley (eng-runtime): Yep I'll add that. Current plan: 1) land kernel-bias patch behind flag 2) add prefetch flag + microbench 3) add deterministic reproducer and nightly trace collection 4) roll to canary. Anyone object?
Mike R.: +1. Add a note to release notes about potential perf diff when aggressive_merge=true.
Lee (ML perf): Please attach the perfetto flame for the nightly once available. If patch reduces KV evictions we should see contiguous KV usage regions.
Ashley (eng-runtime): Thanks all. Pushing PR now: https://git.redwood/pr/eng-runtime/2457 (WIP). I'll post the final nsys + perfetto links after the canary run completes. :thumbsup:
